messages:
sam_sales: FYI acme-health just signed a soft commit — target is ~5M tokens/day with a hard 99th-latency SLO of 350ms. They want reserved GPUs + burst credits and a security questionnaire turnaround this week. Can we sketch sizing and a presales quote? @maya_se @jordan_eng

maya_se: Congrats. Traffic shape from their doc: weekday baseline ~40 rps, morning peak 3x for 20-30m, occasional weekend spike 2x. Median output length ~90 tokens, p95 ~220. They want canary rollout + AZ spread. Also KMS + VPC peering asked in questionnaire.

jordan_eng: Quick back-of-envelope: 5M tokens/day ≈ 57.9 tokens/sec average. With avg 90 tokens per request => ~0.64 req/sec average (~55 rps? wait). Let me reframe: tokens/day -> requests/day estimate = 5,000,000 / 90 ≈ 55,555 req/day → ~0.64 req/sec average. Peak multiplier 3x → peak ~1.9 req/sec average but spike length short; more meaningful is concurrency and token throughput during 30m window. If peak rate is 3x baseline rps: baseline 40 rps → peak 120 rps. At p95 tokens 220 -> token throughput 26,400 tokens/sec at peak.

jordan_eng: For sizing, rule-of-thumb GPU throughput (FP16 / quantized) varies. Example: A8x-class yields ~8-12k tokens/sec per GPU depending on seq len. So for 26k tokens/sec peak we need ≈3 GPUs (conservative: 3-4) for hosting a non-quantized variant. With 8-bit quantization we can reduce to 2-3. Recommend reserved pool of 4 GPUs with a burst pool of 2 extra (burst credits) to handle AZ failover and transient surges.

maya_se: Proposed autoscale policy: min=2 reserved workers, target CPU/GPU util 65-75%, scale step +1 GPU, cooldown 90s, burst pool allowed up to +2 GPUs with prewarm window 5m. Canary: route 5% traffic for 15m then 20%/30m before full 100%.

anna_sre: KV warmup plan: recommend preheat script that runs representative prompts at 1 rps per instance for 10 min prior to the daily peak to populate KV cache. We should also snapshot KV after canary to speed future rollouts. Add a health-check that watches kv_hit_rate and tail latency.

luis_sales: Pricing ask from acme: they expect a 20% discount on reserved commit vs payg and a pool of burst credits. How do we structure commercial terms? Also they want predictable monthly cap.

jordan_eng: Commercially, offer: Reserved: 4 GPUs committed + monthly burst credit bucket of 2 GPU-equivalent hours/day. If they take 12-month commit, offer 18% discount + dedicated support add-on. Technical caveats: if they expect >20% growth, we should add a runway buffer.

maya_se: Security questionnaire flags: KMS integration (BYOK), SOC2 & ISO docs, VPC peering and private CP, audit logs retention 12 months, support for ephemeral logs, HIPAA attestation required per their legal. We need answers for: data residency (EU/US), key rotation policy, and on-prem HSM support.

sam_sales: Action items: 1) Jordan — produce a short 1-page capacity calc + GPU recommendation (include conservative and optimistic numbers) by EOD. 2) Maya — draft autoscale policy + preheat script snippet + canary plan. 3) Anna — fill security questionnaire items flagged and add required artefacts. 4) Luis — propose commercial construct with pricing tiers (monthly committed + burst credits) and caveats.

jordan_eng: I'll drop the calc. Quick snippet I'll include in the doc: ```peak_tokens_per_sec = 120_rps * 220_tokens = 26400 tokens/sec
gpu_tokens_per_sec = 9000  # conservative estimate
gpus_needed = ceil(26400 / 9000)  # = 3
reserved_recommendation = 4  # add 1 for AZ/failover buffer
burst_pool = 2
```

maya_se: sample autoscale JSON for ops to review: ```{
  "min_instances": 2,
  "max_instances": 6,
  "scale_target_util_percent": 70,
  "burst_pool": 2,
  "prewarm_seconds": 300
}```

anna_sre: Also add SLA escape hatch: when queue_length > 5000 or tail_latency > 2x SLO for 3m, trigger cross-region failover and throttle non-critical routes. Document that in runbook.

ops_bot: Deploy reminder: presales-docs/poc/acme-health/capacity_calc_v1.pdf uploaded by jordan_eng at 1758012400

sam_sales: Thanks — once the calc + pricing draft are in I'll sync with acme legal and ops. We should aim to return the security questionnaire answers within 3 business days. :thumbsup:

luis_sales: I'll prepare contract language for the burst credits and cap. Will ping @maya_se for the wording around canary windows.

jordan_eng: Uploading the calc now, will add notes on quantization tradeoffs (bigger quality risk vs cost wins).

maya_se: Ping me if you need a sample prompt set for preheat. I have a small set that mimics their user flows.

sam_sales: Great — wrapping up here. We'll reconvene tomorrow after doc reviews. Thanks all.
